title: Feasibility of ICG labeling of axillary sentinel lymph nodes following neoadjuvant chemotherapy for breast cancer
summary: The aim is to investigate the feasibility of using the fluorescent dye indocyanine green (ICG) for the marking and targeted removal of sentinel lymph nodes in breast cancer patients who have received chemotherapy prior to surgery.  In breast cancer patients undergoing primary surgery, ICG can be used for sentinel lymph node removal with a high success rate and represents a cost-effective and less burdensome alternative to radioactive technetium. Currently, there is very little data on its applicability in patients who first receive chemotherapy. This feasibility study aims to collect such data.

interventions.name:
prospective, single-center, single-arm feasibility study
(Recording of the number of detected sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) intraoperatively/ histologically after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) and ICG labeling, prospectively; comparison of the number of ICG-labeled SLNs removed from the prospective

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
invasive breast cancer
neoadjuvant chemotherapy
indication for SLNB/TAD
written consent
Exclusion criteria:
Iodine allergy
Hyperthyroidism/autonomous thyroid adenomas
Pregnancy/breastfeeding
Hypersensitivity to sodium iodide or ICG
History of axillary surgery
